label: Gregory M. Guillot
narrative: Guillot is the four-star who had to say out loud that the United States cannot identify what is flying over its own nuclear-capable bases. He took command of NORAD and US Northern Command in February 2024 and immediately made counter-unmanned-systems the centrepiece of his 90-day assessment, with the December 2023 Langley Air Force Base incursions as the driving case. Speaking to The War Zone on 30 October 2024 he conceded the limits of what he could say - 'The only thing I can tell you about the Langley drones is roughly the number and roughly the altitude' - and, on the question everyone wanted answered, 'I have not seen [and] I do not know of any organized or unorganized foreign nexus.' NORAD's own figure at that point was more than 600 drone reports over US military installations since 2022. By March 2026, after waves of incursions over Barksdale Air Force Base and other strategic installations following the launch of Operation Epic Fury, Guillot told reporters 'We've seen an increase from last year in the number of detections over military installations,' with roughly a quarter of detected drones now defeated versus almost none previously. Read from the board's premise, Guillot is the honest institutional face of a real gap: the command responsible for homeland air defence is describing an unattributed, persistent, sensor-resistant intrusion campaign against the continental United States and cannot name the actor.
